considered.label: Handbook 1 Program overview
considered.text: 1 Program overview. The B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering runs for four years, each split into two semesters. Years 1 and 2 are all core courses. From Year 3, students add electives and may earn a specialization by focusing their electives on one track. Every course in the catalog belongs to one year and one semester and is offered only in that semester.

considered.label: Handbook 3.3 Failing and repeating a course
considered.text: 3.3 Failing and repeating a course. A failed core course must be repeated the next time it is offered, which is the same semester of the following year. When a failed course is passed on a later attempt, the new grade replaces the F in the CGPA. A course that was passed cannot be repeated to improve the grade.

considered.label: Handbook 4.1 The rule
considered.text: 4.1 The rule. A student may register for a course only after passing every prerequisite listed for it in the catalog, with a grade of P or better. Courses in progress do not count as passed. Some courses also require a minimum number of earned credits, shown in the catalog.
